<thought>Using the retrieved DBE formula DBE = (2C + 2 + N - H - X)/2 and the molecular formula C6H9O2 (C=6, H=9, N=0, X=0), the calculation yields (12 + 2 − 9)/2 = 5/2 = 2.5. Since DBE must be an integer for a neutral molecule, the most plausible integer value is 2 (corresponding to one ring and one double bond, e.g., a lactone).</thought>
<final_answer>2</final_answer>
